topIssues.title: Chain config can't express genesis `minBaseFee`, so nodes started from the registry diverge
topIssues.author: donoso-eth
topIssues.body:
# Chain config can't express genesis `minBaseFee`, so nodes started from the registry diverge

While preparing the registry entry for Whitechain I hit a gap that would split the chain.

Whitechain has Jovian active at genesis with `minBaseFee = 5000000000`. `[genesis.system_config]` has nowhere to put that, so a node started with `--network <chain>` builds the first block after genesis with a `0` floor. `minBaseFee` is part of the block's `extraData`, so that block gets a different hash and derivation diverges at genesis+1.

On chain (`extraData` = `version ‖ denominator ‖ elasticity ‖ minBaseFee`):

```
block 50961390 (genesis)  0x01000000fa000000060000000000000000  minBaseFee 0           baseFee 1000000000
block 50961391            0x01000000fa00000006000000012a05f200  minBaseFee 5000000000  baseFee  996000000
block 50961392            0x01000000fa00000006000000012a05f200  minBaseFee 5000000000  baseFee 5000000000
```

Genesis+1 is still on the genesis L1 origin, so the floor can't come from an L1 `ConfigUpdate` — it comes from the genesis system config, which is exactly what the registry drops.

And it drops it silently: with `minBaseFee` in the staged config, `sync_staging --check` still reports `validation successful` and the key is gone after promotion.

The same applies to the operator fee params and `daFootprintGasScalar`. They go into the L1 attributes deposit instead of `extraData`, but a wrong value changes the block hash just the same. Whitechain has those at zero, so only `minBaseFee` bites today.

## Proposal

Add the four fields to `[genesis.system_config]` as optional keys (kona already models all of them, so the names can follow it). Nothing shipped today changes.

Recommended follow-up, separate from the fix: reject unknown keys in staged configs instead of ignoring them. Everything downstream already decodes strictly; the registry is the only lenient step, which is why the drop above was silent.

The monorepo needs the matching change before a config with these keys is promoted, otherwise its strict decode fails on the next pin bump. kona and op-reth need nothing.

I have the registry PR ready.

(#1093/#1165 added `minBaseFee` to the staging report and the standard range check, but those read the current on-chain value, not the genesis one.)

topPRs.title: feat: add Whitechain Sepolia Testnet
topPRs.author: donoso-eth
topPRs.body:
> **Do not merge until #1399 and the matching monorepo PR are merged.** This config sets `minBaseFee`, which the registry schema only models after #1399 (this branch is stacked on it — the diff shrinks to the two staging files once it lands). Promoting it before the monorepo models the field would fail `TestAllEmbeddedConfigsDecodeStrictly` on the next pin bump. See #1398.

Adds Whitechain Sepolia Testnet (chain ID 1874) to the registry.

| | |
|---|---|
| Chain ID | 1874 |
| Superchain | sepolia |
| Contracts | op-contracts/v6.0.0 (L1 + L2), permissioned games only |
| DA | eth-da |
| Block time | 1s |
| Gas limit | 40,000,000 |
| Genesis `minBaseFee` | 5 gwei (Jovian at genesis) |
| Governed by Optimism | no |
| Public RPC | https://rpc.testnet.whitechain.io |
| Explorer | https://explorer.testnet.whitechain.io |

### Verified against chain

- **L2 genesis**: hash `0xb92575f4…`, L1 origin 11071328 (`0x6a6d405d…`), batcher, packed scalar (1368 / 801949) and gas limit all match the staged config. Genesis artifact round-trips byte-identically.
- **`minBaseFee`**: `SystemConfig.minBaseFee()` reads `5000000000` on L1, and the L2's `extraData` carries it from block 1 onward (block 0 has `0`, so it's the genesis system config, not a later `ConfigUpdate`).
- **Roles and addresses**: `SystemConfig` owner/batcher/unsafe-signer and all six contract getters, `OptimismPortal.guardian()`, `ProxyAdmin.owner()`, and the proposer/challenger/vm/weth decoded from `DisputeGameFactory.gameArgs(1)` all match. `respectedGameType = 1`; no permissionless game registered.
- **Contract versions**: every proxy reports its v6.0.0 standard version (SystemConfig 3.13.1, Portal 5.2.0, DGF 1.4.0, ASR 3.7.0, DelayedWETH 1.5.0, PDG 2.2.0). SystemConfig and DGF resolve to the standard Sepolia impl addresses byte-for-byte.

### Notes for the reviewer

- **Own SuperchainConfig, as expected for a non-governed chain.** The chain uses its own `SuperchainConfig` (`0x11854D31…`) and its own v6.0.0 OPCM instance (`0xe259c6ea…`) rather than the Sepolia superchain's. Both are canonical v6.0.0 — the `SuperchainConfig` proxies to the standard `0xb08cc720…` implementation.
- **Impl addresses that differ from the standard table.** Portal, ASR, DelayedWETH, PreimageOracle and MIPS sit on non-standard implementations purely because their constructor args carry testnet-length windows (proof maturity 15 min, finality delay 5 min, withdrawal delay 10 min, challenge period 5 min). Every contract whose args weren't overridden — SystemConfig, DisputeGameFactory, SuperchainConfig — lands on the standard v6.0.0 impl byte-for-byte.
- **Prestate.** `gameArgs(1)` registers the generic op-program 1.3.1 cannon32 prestate, which predates this chain and can't prove it. Fine for a permissioned game; needs a custom prestate before any permissionless game type is enabled.
- **Filename.** Staged as `wch-sepolia.toml` because `check_chainlist` compares the staged filename against the ethereum-lists `shortName` (`wch-sepolia`). If you'd prefer `whitechain.toml` at promotion (→ `--network whitechain-sepolia`), please rename then.

topPRs.title: ops: carry post-Isthmus/Jovian genesis system config params
topPRs.author: donoso-eth
topPRs.body:
Closes #1398

## What

`[genesis.system_config]` can't express `minBaseFee` or the other post-Isthmus genesis params. For a Jovian-at-genesis chain with a non-zero floor, a node started from the registry builds genesis+1 with a `0` floor and diverges — see #1398 for the on-chain evidence.

## Changes

- `config.SystemConfig`: add `operatorFeeScalar`, `operatorFeeConstant`, `minBaseFee`, `daFootprintGasScalar` as optional keys. Names match kona's `SystemConfig`, which already models all four.
- `create-config` carries them from `rollup.Genesis.SystemConfig`, recorded only when non-zero (absent and zero are equivalent downstream).
- Docs: the new keys in the custom-chain template.

## Verification

- `apply_hardforks` rewrites all 55 shipped configs through the new struct: byte-identical, `git status` clean.
- New tests: fields round-trip when set and are omitted when unset; `create-config` carries non-zero values and skips zeros.

## Sequencing

Safe to merge alone — no shipped config sets the new keys. A config that does must not be promoted until the monorepo models them (`op-core` `SystemConfig` + `LoadOPStackRollupConfig`), or `TestAllEmbeddedConfigsDecodeStrictly` fails the next pin bump. Monorepo PR to follow.

## Recommended follow-up

Staged configs are decoded leniently, which is why a `minBaseFee` key passes `sync_staging --check` with `validation successful` and would be dropped at promotion. Downstream consumers (op-core, kona) all decode strictly. Rejecting unknown keys at staging time would catch the next unmodeled field or typo before it ships; kept out of this PR to keep it to the fix.

topPRs.title: ops: reject unknown keys when decoding registry TOML
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #1403. This is the follow-up it recommends.

## What

The ops tooling decoded registry TOML leniently. A key the Go structs don't model was silently dropped, and then lost when the config was rewritten on promotion. That is how #1398 got through: a staged `minBaseFee` passed `sync_staging --check` with `validation successful` and disappeared, while every downstream consumer (op-core, kona) decodes strictly.

After this PR, an unknown key fails the read and names the key:

```
failed to read .../.staging/wch-sepolia.toml: unknown TOML keys not represented in the target struct: genesis.system_config.minBaseFee
```

## Changes

- `paths.ReadTOMLFile` decodes with op-service's `jsonutil.DecodeTOMLStrict`, which the registry already uses for hardforks validation. It covers staged chain configs, staged and shipped `superchain.toml`, and the standard config params.
- The remaining direct `toml.Unmarshal` readers of registry configs use the same strict decode: `manage.CollectChainConfigs`, `manage.ReadChainConfig` and `paths.SuperchainIds`. That covers shipped configs too, so a key added by hand under `superchain/configs/` is caught.
- `config.SuperchainDefinition` gains `safer_safes_addr`, which `mainnet`/`sepolia` `superchain.toml` have carried since #1197. op-core already models it; the registry's own struct didn't. Nil pointers aren't encoded, and `WriteSuperchainDefinition` never overwrites an existing file, so generated output doesn't change.
- Removed a stale `deployment_tx_hash` from the `testchain.toml` test fixture. It's a staging-only field that shipped configs never have.

## Verification

- `TestConfigReadersRejectUnknownKeys` and `TestReadTOMLFile_RejectsUnknownKeys` fail on the #1403 base and pass here. They cover the decoder and each reader: staged chain, staged superchain, collected chain configs, and chain config by name.
- `TestShippedConfigsDecodeStrictly` strictly decodes every shipped `superchain.toml` and chain config (7 superchains, 63 chains). It fails with `safer_safes_addr` when that field is removed.
- `apply_hardforks` rewrites everything through the strict path with no diff. `check-chainlist` and `check-genesis-integrity` pass. Both `standard-config-params-*.toml` decode strictly into `validation.ConfigParams`.
- Replayed every staged config ever committed on a PR branch that I have locally (29 versions). The 2025 drafts carried keys the schema no longer has (`superchain_level`, `hardforks.interop_time`, `regolith_time`, roles under `[addresses]`, `protocol_versions_addr`), all of which were silently dropped. The most recent, `wch-sepolia` (2026-11), is the #1398 `minBaseFee` case. On this stack it decodes cleanly; without #1403 it is rejected.
- `go vet ./...` is clean. Local golangci-lint can't load the Go 1.26 module (the pinned 1.64.8 is a Go 1.23 build), so lint is left to CI. `TestBinaryInvocation`, `TestScanL2` and `TestVersionsIntegrity` need RPC and cache env vars, so they run in CI only.

## Merge order

Merge after #1403. Without it, staged configs that set the new genesis fields are rejected. That is the intended behaviour, but it would block chains that need them.
